solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disaster area engulfed by threat cops dealt with (11)

indicators.note: A is swallowed up inside the rearranged letters
the letters of THREAT COPS are dealt out afresh, like a hand of cards

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area
the ten letters to be rearranged around A

annotation.surface: Police officers handle a menace in some stricken zone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disaster area' reads as one phrase, but only 'Disaster' is the definition; 'area' is the A that goes into the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a catastrophe is a sudden event causing great damage or suffering.

clue.text: Basis for lying to head off complaints being raised (3)

indicators.note: the head taken off 'complaints' is its first letter
in a down clue, raising something turns it upside down

blocks.note: used as it stands
first letter of COMPLAINTS

annotation.surface: A liar's grounds for fibbing: getting in first to stop people grumbling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' pretends to mean telling fibs; here it means lying down, and a cot is a bed to lie on.
annotation.definitionFit: A cot is a small bed, the thing you lie on.

clue.text: Upset by books concerned with material unsuitable for consumption (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read 'by' as in three by four
OT = Old Testament, a set of books
as in 'a specialist in law'

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed by books about inedible stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an emotion in the surface; it only turns X and OT over.
annotation.definitionFit: A toxin is poison, something you must not eat or drink.

clue.text: Time spent with relations? (3,4)

blocks.note: the surface reading: hours passed with family members, aunts and cousins
the meant reading: relations as in sexual relations, the part of life spent in bed with a partner

annotation.surface: Hours passed in the company of the family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relations' makes you think of aunts and cousins; the question mark flags the other sense, sexual relations.
annotation.definitionFit: Your sex life is the part of life spent having sexual relations.

clue.text: Look back on timid people adopting new lives (9)

indicators.note: MICE take N and IS into their family, so those letters go inside

blocks.note: RE = regarding, on the subject of
a timid person is called a mouse
N = new
to live is to exist, to be: he lives = he is

annotation.surface: Thinking over a story in which shy people take in new lives, as if adopting children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives' is the noun in the surface and the verb in the wordplay: 'he lives' means 'he is'. 'On' goes at the front of the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reminisce is to recall past times fondly, looking back over them.

clue.text: Don backing away from university? (3,2)

indicators.note: going backwards, so NOT UP is read in reverse

blocks.note: British students are 'up' at university, so being away is being NOT UP

annotation.surface: A university don retreating from his college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, which the surface leans on; it is the verb meaning to put clothes on. At Oxford and Cambridge a student goes 'up' to university and 'down' at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to don clothing is to dress in it, as you would a hat or coat.

clue.text: Record conclusion of economist in key message (7)

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter
'in key' places the economist's final letter within the island word, as a thing sits in a place

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
last letter of ECONOMIST

annotation.surface: Noting down an economist's final point in an important memo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key message' suggests a main point; 'key' is really a small island, a sense solvers often miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a formal flavour: epistle is the old word for a letter, as in the New Testament letters of Paul.

clue.text: Sum up child’s parent having no boundaries (3)

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters, which go

blocks.note: what a small child calls a father

annotation.surface: Assessing a parent who sets their child no limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Child's' matters: not just DAD but the child's word DADDY, whose ends D and Y are dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to sum up figures is to total them, finding what they come to together.

clue.text: Top and tail without starting off at opposite ends (9)

indicators.note: take away the letter that starts the phrase
the letters go off, gone wrong, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: TOPANDTAIL with its starting T removed

annotation.surface: An instruction to trim something at both ends, without the first step being started.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top and tail' is a British phrase for trimming the ends off vegetables; here it is just the letters to be used.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipodal means on the directly opposite side of the globe, at opposite ends.

clue.text: In fact, I’m hesitant to adopt incidental requirement (11)

indicators.note: the result goes in the word for fact
ER adopts SIDE, taking it inside

blocks.note: a datum is a single fact
the sound a hesitant speaker makes
as in a side issue

annotation.surface: Someone admits reluctance to take on some minor requirement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In fact' looks like a throwaway phrase; 'In' puts everything inside DATUM.
annotation.definitionFit: A desideratum is something needed or wanted, a requirement.

clue.text: Invite hosts to cancel social media platform relieved of duties? (3-6)

indicators.note: TEMPT hosts, holding the other letters inside

blocks.note: to invite trouble is to tempt it
to axe a project is to cancel it
X is the platform formerly called Twitter

annotation.surface: An invitation to drop a social media site, after someone is released from work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duties' suggests jobs to do; the question mark flags its other sense, taxes.
annotation.definitionFit: Tax-exempt means relieved of paying duties, that is, taxes.

clue.text: Sudden attack [by] America on international court (5)

indicators.note: in an across clue, US placed on ICT follows it

blocks.note: I = international
CT is the abbreviation for court
US = America

annotation.surface: A news line about America striking at the International Criminal Court.
annotation.walkthrough: An ictus is a medical term for a sudden attack such as a stroke or seizure.
annotation.definitionFit: Ictus is the medical word for a sudden seizure or stroke.

clue.text: Writer’s article not free of charge [or] regular payment (7)

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, so the pen's
an ion is a particle that carries an electric charge

annotation.surface: An author's piece that is not given away free, or else a regular fee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not free of charge' reads as 'costs money'; it means electrically charged, which describes an ion.
annotation.definitionFit: Defined by its nature: money paid out weekly or monthly to someone after they retire from work.

clue.text: Reconstruction of state involved Speaker suppressing anarchic riot (11)

indicators.note: tangled up, so SPEAKER is rearranged
the rearranged SPEAKER holds the other letters down inside it
in disorder, so RIOT is rearranged

blocks.note: rearranged to PERES...KA
rearranged to TROI

annotation.surface: A parliamentary Speaker keeps a lid on a chaotic riot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' looks like the parliamentary officer; it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's restructuring of the Soviet state in the 1980s.

clue.text: Writer’s block? (7)

blocks.note: the surface reading: an author's inability to get any words down
the meant reading: a block of paper sheets that a writer jots on

annotation.walkthrough: Writer's block is the inability to write; read literally, it is a block of paper that a writer uses.
annotation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of paper sheets for writing notes.

clue.text: Rob once close to those in party (5)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter
'in party' means inside the party word, as a guest is in a party

blocks.note: a rave is a large dance party
last letter of THOSE

annotation.surface: A man called Rob, once close to certain people in a political party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a man's name; it is the verb. 'Once' marks an old-fashioned word.
annotation.definitionFit: To reave is an archaic word for to rob or plunder.

clue.text: Who tried to transform contents of project cherished by top people? (9)

indicators.note: what is inside a word, without its outer letters
held close, so A-LIST holds CHEM

blocks.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities
SCHEME is a project; its contents are CHEM

annotation.surface: Asking which person tried to change the aims of a project beloved of the bosses.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because alchemists tried to transform base metals into gold. 'Project' must first become SCHEME.
annotation.definitionFit: An alchemist tried to transform base metals into gold.

clue.text: Resignation relatively certain to include distress (9)

indicators.note: SURER includes REND inside it

blocks.note: the comparative of sure, certain relative to something
to rend is to tear, and also to distress or wrench the heart

annotation.surface: Stepping down from a job is fairly sure to bring some anguish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' is the comparative: relatively certain is 'surer', not 'fairly sure'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: resignation here is the act of giving in, handing oneself over to defeat.

clue.text: Dog soldiers snubbed orderly continually (9)

indicators.note: snub-nosed, so the word's end is cut short

blocks.note: RE = Royal Engineers
TRIM (neat, orderly) with its last letter cut off
as in 'ever hopeful'

annotation.surface: Soldiers keep cold-shouldering a dogged orderly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like the military attendant the soldiers ignore; it is the adjective, TRIM.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Labrador and golden varieties are gun dogs bred to fetch shot game.

clue.text: Told to go to collect advanced study [for] confirmation? (9)

indicators.note: SENT collects the other letters inside it

blocks.note: if you are sent, you are told to go
A = advanced
to cram is to study hard

annotation.surface: Someone is told to go and pick up advanced coursework as proof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Confirmation' looks like proof; the question mark points to the church rite. The question mark signals that confirmation is only one example of a sacrament.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: confirmation is a church rite, one of several alongside baptism and communion.

clue.text: Keen promoter possibly bitter about appointment (7)

indicators.note: ALE goes about, around, POST

blocks.note: bitter is a type of British beer, so an example of ale
a post is a job someone is appointed to

annotation.surface: An enthusiastic promoter may be resentful over a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like an adjective about feelings; it is the British pale beer, so 'possibly' makes it an example of ALE.
annotation.definitionFit: An extended sense: from the twelve who spread Christ's teaching comes any zealous advocate of a cause.

clue.text: Leave / divided / city (5)

blocks.note: slang for depart, as in 'let's get out of here'
cut into parts, as a vote or a log can be
a port city on the Adriatic coast of Croatia

annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions rather than two: the third is Split, the Croatian port city.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for leaving, the past participle for divided, and the name of a Croatian city.

clue.text: Fixed charge securing queen[’s] release (3,4)

indicators.note: SET FEE holds R securely inside it

blocks.note: a set fee is a fixed charge
R = Regina, Latin for queen

annotation.surface: A fixed payment secures the queen's freedom, like a ransom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a ransom demand for a queen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: releasing a captive means letting them go at liberty.

clue.text: Recite fluently [with] feel for performing (4,3)

indicators.note: the letters perform, putting on a new show

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: An actor delivers lines smoothly with a real feel for the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Performing' fits the actor picture so well that it reads as scenery; it is the instruction to rearrange 'feel for'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to rattle a list off quickly without pausing, as a fishing line runs off a spinning reel.

clue.text: Stood up to knock back drink (5)

indicators.note: 'back' carries the instruction: the drink word is knocked backwards, read from its end

blocks.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

annotation.surface: Someone got to their feet to down a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' wants to mean gulp down the drink; it only turns DECAF round.
annotation.definitionFit: To face an enemy is to stand up to them.

clue.text: Acting head of IT plugs trendy expression (7)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
I plugs a gap inside TERM

blocks.note: in = fashionable
a term is a word or expression
first letter of IT

annotation.surface: A stand-in IT boss promotes a fashionable buzzword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acting head' looks like one phrase, a temporary boss; only 'Acting' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An interim manager is an acting one, holding the post temporarily.

clue.text: River horse released from trap (5)

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so what comes out of it is spoken

blocks.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs

annotation.surface: A horse escapes from a trap and makes for the river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trap' suggests a pony and trap; it is British slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of Switzerland and France.

clue.text: Setter would jot down answer [for] fool (5)

indicators.note: IOTA goes down by the answer, losing the A

blocks.note: the setter is I, so 'I would' is I'D
a jot or iota is a tiny amount
A = answer, the letter removed

annotation.surface: The compiler would note the solution for some fool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jot down' looks like 'write down'; 'jot' is the noun IOTA and 'down answer' means minus A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a stupid person, used as an insult.

clue.text: Yawning doctor uncovers insomnia finally (9)

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
take the final letter of INSOMNIA

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
last letter of INSOMNIA

annotation.surface: A drowsy physician discovers that a patient has insomnia at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yawning' fits the insomnia story as tiredness; it means gaping wide, and 'doctor' is the verb, not the physician.
annotation.definitionFit: A yawning gap is a cavernous one, huge and open.

clue.text: Drunk husband left out of photograph (3)

indicators.note: H is left out, removed from the word

blocks.note: H = husband, the letter removed
a shot is a photo

annotation.surface: A drunken husband was left out of the family picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is the noun, a drunkard, not the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with drunk as a noun: someone habitually intoxicated, a drunkard.

clue.text: Bug delaying final stage of deployment [is] likely (3)

indicators.note: the T is held back and arrives last
the final stage of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: to bug a phone is to tap it
last letter of DEPLOYMENT, the T that moves

annotation.surface: A software glitch holding up the last phase of a rollout is probable.
annotation.walkthrough: The T of TAP is also the last letter of 'deployment', so delaying it moves it to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Apt to happen means likely to happen.

clue.text: Sanction / record racing driver deserved? (11)

blocks.note: approval, as in the board's sanction of a plan
in Britain a motoring offence such as speeding is written onto the driver's licence as penalty points

annotation.walkthrough: 'Racing driver' means a speeding motorist, not a Formula One star. 'Sanction' can mean both approval and a penalty.
annotation.definitionFit: An endorsement is approval, and also a penalty noted on a driving licence.
